events.title: The election of Pope Paul VI
events.shortBlurb: Giovanni Battista Montini was chosen to carry the Second Vatican Council to its conclusion…
body: On 21 June 1963, eighteen days after the death of John XXIII, the cardinals elected on the sixth ballot Giovanni Battista Montini, Archbishop of Milan, who took the name Paul VI. Born at Concesio near Brescia in 1897, he had served some thirty years in the Secretariat of State before going to Milan in 1954.

His coronation on 30 June 1963 was the last in papal history. He brought the Second Vatican Council, interrupted by John's death, through three more sessions to its close on 8 December 1965, and then governed the long labor of putting its decrees into effect, including the reform of the liturgy.

The first pope in modern times to travel outside Italy, he journeyed to the Holy Land in 1964 and addressed the United Nations in 1965. His encyclical Humanae Vitae of 1968 met widespread dissent. He died at Castel Gandolfo on 6 August 1978 and was canonized by Pope Francis in 2018.

sources.text: Vatican biography, Canonization of St. Paul VI (vatican.va)
